ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that diamond $ABCD$ has a side length of 2, and $\angle BAD=60^\circ$. If $DE\perp AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular at point $E$, then what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE \perp AB$,\\
hence $\angle AED = 90^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle ADE$, given $\angle BAD = 60^\circ$, and $AD = 2$,\\
hence $\sin60^\circ = \frac{DE}{AD}$,\\
thus $DE = AD \cdot \sin60^\circ = 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

Reasoning: The side length of rhombus ABCD is 2, so AD = 2. Because E is on AB, in triangle ADE, ∠DAE is ∠BAD, which is 60°. Also because DE ⟂ AB, ∠AED = 90°, triangle ADE is a right triangle, AD is the hypotenuse, and DE is the side opposite the 60° angle. Therefore sin 60° = DE / AD, obtaining DE = AD · sin 60° = 2 · (√3/2) = √3.

method.method_draft: Use the right triangle formed by the altitude. First describe the diagram: the image shows rhombus/diamond ABCD with A at the left, B above, C to the right, D below, and segment DE drawn from D to meet line AB at E. From the text, take that every side of the diamond has length 2, so AD=2, that angle BAD is 60°, and that DE is perpendicular to AB. Then in right triangle ADE, AD is the hypotenuse and DE is opposite the 60° angle at A. Apply sin 60° = DE/AD, so DE = 2·sin 60° = √3.

method.method_draft: Use the area of the rhombus as a parallelogram. First describe the diagram: the image shows ABCD as a slanted diamond with AB usable as a base and DE drawn from D perpendicular to AB, so DE is the height corresponding to base AB. From the text, the rhombus has side length 2, so AB=AD=2, and the included angle between AB and AD is angle BAD=60°. Compute the rhombus area using adjacent sides: area = AB·AD·sin 60° = 2·2·√3/2 = 2√3. The same area using base AB and height DE is area = AB·DE = 2·DE. Equate 2·DE = 2√3, giving DE=√3.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The figure shows a slanted diamond/rhombus ABCD, with A on the left, B near the top, C on the right, and D near the bottom. Segment AB can be viewed as a base. A segment DE is drawn from D to point E on line AB, and the problem states DE is perpendicular to AB, so DE is the height corresponding to base AB. Reasoning: Since ABCD is a rhombus with side length 2, AB = AD = 2. The included angle between adjacent sides AB and AD is angle BAD = 60°. Using the parallelogram/rhombus area formula with adjacent sides, area = AB × AD × sin 60° = 2 × 2 × √3/2 = 2√3. Using base AB and height DE, the same area is area = AB × DE = 2 × DE. Equating the two expressions gives 2DE = 2√3, so DE = √3.
